newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki slips as caution lingers, Neste eases.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki slips as caution lingers, Neste eases.

text.p: Shares fell across the board on Friday on continued international weakness caused by U.S. Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's warnings on Wednesday, brokers said.
But trade was thin and some said there market had technical support in the FOX index of the most traded blue-chips.
"The market does not look weak as long as the FOX-index remains above 1,000 points," said one broker.
The FOX index fell 1.17 percent to close at 1,016.53 points, more than the HEX general index which ended 0.91 percent down at 2,893.49 points. Volume was under 500 million markka.

Profit-taking hit oil and chemicals group Neste despite in-line 1996 earnings -- before the results the share had risen 20 percent this month and 30 percent this year. Brokers also said its dividend was lower than expected and the share closed fair trade down 4.00 markka at 140.00.
Telecoms group Nokia fell with U.S. technology stocks, down 5.50 markka at 303.50.
Some small caps were among outperformers, helped perhaps by end-month window dressing, brokers said.
Plastic pipes and furniture group Asko rose 8.00 markka to 420.00 after Thursday's healthy 1996 report.

Refocussed engineering group Partek extended recent gains with a 1.50 markka rise to 83.50 markka, with demand boosted by recent analyst comments, brokers said. Nokian Renkaat also stayed strong on overseas demand after its strong 1996 report two weeks ago -- up 2.00 at 137.00 markka.
Paper machine maker Valmet slipped 2.20 to 91.50 markka on profit-taking, and forestries ended in negative territory although the sub-index touched a record intra-day.
Forestry reports would be in focus next week with UPM- Kymmene due on Tuesday and Enso due on Monday the week after, brokers said.
